Every action the game binds is one row — default codes, a name, a group, whether it is held

a key another action answers is refused by its holder's name, the rail's letters (E · R · L · G · C · T · V · X · P · U — the world's own prompt labels, printed beside what they do) and the build bar's digits are refused as what they are, Esc and Enter stand fixed, and a reset hands every key back to the Order's print
A rebind is a data change persisted in the player's options (`waylight.keys`), never a code path: click a cap in the manual, press a key, and the cap that LISTENED reads the new key
Lessons and the rail read with YOUR keys: `KEYS.say` rewrites every `KEY` token in a lesson to the cap that answers it now, and the rail's E is the interact cap wherever it was bound.
Four tabs on LEDGERLIGHT paper.

figure.note: the manual's tabs read Controls, Lessons, Windows, Saves

clauses.text: CONTROLS from the registry, grouped THE WALK / THE HANDS / THE PAPERS

LESSONS — every page the road has taught, in full, with a search over the walked ones; the unwalked stay SEALED ("a page not yet walked"), so discovery is kept and re-reading is allowed; the count is printed.
LESSONS — all thirty-four pages, walked in full, sealed otherwise, searchable, counted

figure.note: ninety-seven pages at v3.51; the Lessons tab lists all ninety-seven and counts the walked (3 of 97)

clauses.text: THE PAPERS — every sheet the Order keeps (`PAPERS` registry: name, what it is, how it opens) with an OPEN that steps out of the manual
slots 2 and 3 stand beside it; the chosen slot is the player's, persisted with the options, never the porter's
and choosing one reloads the drift behind the menu
RETURN TO THE TITLE from the pause sheet saves this valley and steps out
and CONTINUE walks back in
A PASSAGE CODE is a valley as text: the save deflated (`CompressionStream('deflate-raw')`, a third of the page) and base64'd under a WL1 seal, or plain under WL0 where a browser cannot deflate

figure.note: the WL1 code runs under half the save's length; a third itself is not pinned

clauses.text: import validates the seal, the bytes and the page (a valley has a version, stations and a bank), STASHES whatever the target slot held in its backup first — the no-purge law — and refuses by name with nothing written otherwise
In play, a code imports only into another valley
rides a CSS zoom on the reading surfaces only
the world and the HUD meters untouched, sheets held inside the viewport
THE COURT reads `live`: nine banners in the field, the Iron Giants under a RUMOUR seal
